en bille.explanation: "En bille" means "a beetle". The ending "bille" is also in names of kinds of beetle, as in "en løbebille" (a ground beetle).

en billedhugger.explanation: "En billedhugger" means "a sculptor". It is built from "et billede" (a picture) and "at hugge" (to chop), so literally it is a picture chopper.

en billet.explanation: "En billet" means "a ticket". A very common phrase is "at bestille en billet" (to book a ticket): "Vi har bestilt billetter til koncerten" (We have booked tickets for the concert).

en billetautomat.explanation: "En billetautomat" means "a ticket machine". It is built from "billet" (ticket) and "automat" (machine).

en billetkontrollør.explanation: "En billetkontrollør" means "a ticket inspector". It is built from "billet" (ticket) and "kontrollør" (inspector).

en bilnøgle.explanation: "En bilnøgle" means "a car key". The first part "bil" (car) is also at the start of other words, such as "en bilvask" (a car wash) and "en bilulykke" (a car accident).

en bilulykke.explanation: "En bilulykke" means "a car accident". It is built from "bil" (car) and "ulykke" (accident). To say someone was in one, a very common phrase is "at komme ud for en bilulykke": "Han kom ud for en bilulykke i sidste uge" (He was in a car accident last week).

en bilvask.explanation: "En bilvask" means "a car wash". It is built from "bil" (car) and "vask" (wash).

en bindestreg.explanation: "En bindestreg" means "a hyphen". It is built from "at binde" (to tie) and "en streg" (a line), so literally it is a line that ties words together. The longer line is "en tankestreg" (a dash). To mark an extra remark in the middle of a sentence, use the dash: "Min bror – han bor i Aarhus – kommer i morgen" (My brother – he lives in Aarhus – is coming tomorrow).

en biograf.explanation: "En biograf" means "a movie theater". To say you go to the movies, use "at gå i biografen": "Skal vi i biografen i aften?" (Shall we go to the movies tonight?) The short form "bio" also exists: "Vi går i bio" (We are going to the movies).

en biografi.explanation: "En biografi" means "a biography". When a person writes about his or her own life, the word is "en selvbiografi" (an autobiography): "Hun har skrevet en selvbiografi" (She has written an autobiography).

en biolog.explanation: "En biolog" means "a biologist". The ending "-log" is also in other words for experts, such as "en psykolog" (a psychologist) and "en geolog" (a geologist).

en birk.explanation: "En birk" means "a birch". The word is also joined with "et træ" (a tree) to make "et birketræ" (a birch tree).

en bivirkning.explanation: "En bivirkning" means "a side effect". It is built from "bi-" (side) and "en virkning" (an effect). The same "bi-" is in "et bijob" (a side job).

en bjergbestigning.explanation: "En bjergbestigning" means "a mountain climb". It is built from "et bjerg" (a mountain) and "en bestigning" (a climb), which comes from the verb "at bestige" (to climb up).

en bjørn.explanation: "En bjørn" means "a bear". To name a polar bear, join "is" (ice) and "bjørn": "en isbjørn" (a polar bear).

en blanding.explanation: "En blanding" means "a mixture". A very common phrase is "en blanding af" (a mixture of): "Vi købte en blanding af nødder" (We bought a mixture of nuts).

en blanket.explanation: "En blanket" means "a form", as in a document with empty fields to fill in. To say you hand it in, use "at aflevere" (to hand in): "Du skal aflevere blanketten i morgen" (You have to hand in the form tomorrow).

en ble.explanation: "En ble" means "a diaper". To say you change a diaper, use "at skifte" (to change): "Vil du skifte bleen?" (Will you change the diaper?)

en blender.explanation: "En blender" means "a blender". It is borrowed from the English word "blender".

en blikkenslager.explanation: "En blikkenslager" means "a plumber". It is built from "blik" (tin plate) and "at slå" (to hit), so literally it is someone who hits tin plate.

en blodprop.explanation: "En blodprop" means "a blood clot". When the clot is in the head, say "en blodprop i hjernen" (a stroke). When it is in the heart, say "en blodprop i hjertet" (a heart attack).

en blodprøve.explanation: "En blodprøve" means "a blood test". It is built from "blod" (blood) and "en prøve" (a sample). To say a nurse takes your blood, you say you "have it taken": "Jeg skal have taget en blodprøve" (I have to have a blood test taken).

en blodåre.explanation: "En blodåre" means "a blood vessel". It is built from "blod" (blood) and "en åre" (a vein). A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart is "en pulsåre" (an artery): "Lægen mærker på pulsåren i halsen" (The doctor feels the artery in the neck).

en blog.explanation: "En blog" means "a blog". To say someone writes a blog, use the verb "at blogge" (to blog): "Hun blogger om mad" (She blogs about food).

en blok.explanation: "En blok" means "a notepad". The word also means "a block" of something solid, as in "en isblok" (a block of ice).

en blomme.explanation: "En blomme" means "a plum". Do not mix it up with "en blomst" (a flower). To say you eat a plum, say "Jeg spiser en blomme" (I eat a plum). To say you pick a flower, say "Jeg plukker en blomst" (I pick a flower).

en blomst.explanation: "En blomst" means "a flower". At the start of compound words it takes the form "blomster-", as in "en blomsterbutik" (a flower shop) and "en blomstervase" (a flower vase).

en blomsterbuket.explanation: "En blomsterbuket" means "a bouquet". To say it in a shorter way, use "en buket" (a bouquet): "Hun fik en buket til sin fødselsdag" (She got a bouquet for her birthday).

en blomsterhandler.explanation: "En blomsterhandler" means "a florist". The word also means the shop: "Jeg går forbi blomsterhandleren" (I am walking past the florist's).

en blondine.explanation: "En blondine" means "a blonde". To describe a man or any other person, use the adjective "blond": "en blond mand" (a blond man).

en bluse.explanation: "En bluse" means "a blouse". Do not mix it up with "en skjorte" (a shirt): "Han har en skjorte på" (He is wearing a shirt).

en blyant.explanation: "En blyant" means "a pencil". To say you sharpen a pencil, use "at spidse" (to sharpen): "Jeg spidser min blyant" (I am sharpening my pencil).

en blæksprutte.explanation: "En blæksprutte" means "an octopus / squid". Danish uses one word for both animals. To say which one, add the number of arms: "en ottearmet blæksprutte" (an octopus) and "en tiarmet blæksprutte" (a squid). It is built from "blæk" (ink) and "at sprutte" (to squirt).

en blære.explanation: "En blære" means "a bladder". It also means "a blister" on the skin from a burn, as in "en brandblære" (a burn blister).

en blødning.explanation: "En blødning" means "a bleeding". To say the blood stays inside the body, use "en indre blødning" (internal bleeding).

en bodega.explanation: "En bodega" means "a local bar". The word comes from Spanish "bodega" (a wine cellar or shop).

en bodylotion.explanation: "En bodylotion" means "a body lotion". It is borrowed from English. To say you put it on all over, use "at smøre sig ind" (to rub oneself all over): "Jeg smører mig ind i bodylotion" (I rub body lotion all over myself).

en bog.explanation: "En bog" means "a book". To say you read a book, use "at læse" (to read): "Jeg læser en bog hver aften" (I read a book every evening).

en boghandel.explanation: "En boghandel" means "a bookstore". It is built from "bog" (book) and "handel" (trade). Do not mix it up with "et bibliotek" (a library), where you borrow books: "Jeg låner bogen på biblioteket" (I borrow the book at the library).

en boghandler.explanation: "En boghandler" means "a bookseller". The word also means the shop: "Jeg går forbi boghandleren" (I am walking past the bookstore).

en bold.explanation: "En bold" means "a ball". To say you play with a ball, use "at spille bold" (to play ball): "Børnene spiller bold i haven" (The children are playing ball in the garden).

en bolig.explanation: "En bolig" means "a home", as in a place to live. To say someone has no permanent place to live, say "Han har ingen fast bolig" (He has no permanent home). Do not mix it up with "et hjem" (a home with a feeling of belonging): "Vi har et rart hjem" (We have a lovely home).

en boligblok.explanation: "En boligblok" means "an apartment block". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "en blok" (a block).

en boligforening.explanation: "En boligforening" means "a housing association". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "en forening" (an association). In Denmark, "en almen boligforening" is a non-profit one that rents out homes.

en boligkarré.explanation: "En boligkarré" means "a city block". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "en karré" (a block of buildings).

en bolle.explanation: "En bolle" means "a bun". It also means a meatball in the dish "boller i karry" (meatballs in curry): "Vi spiser boller i karry til middag" (We are eating meatballs in curry for dinner).

en bombe.explanation: "En bombe" means "a bomb". To say someone threatens to use a bomb, use "en bombetrussel" (a bomb threat), built from "bombe" and "en trussel" (a threat): "Skolen fik en bombetrussel" (The school got a bomb threat).

en bon.explanation: "En bon" means "a receipt". To say you keep it, use "at gemme" (to keep): "Gem bonen, hvis du vil bytte varen" (Keep the receipt if you want to exchange the item).

en bonde.explanation: "En bonde" means "a farmer". A different meaning of the same word is "a pawn" in chess: "Jeg flytter en bonde" (I move a pawn).

en bonus.explanation: "En bonus" means "a bonus". To say you receive one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en bonus i december" (I got a bonus in December).

en bordplade.explanation: "En bordplade" means "a tabletop / countertop". Danish uses one word for both. It is built from "bord" (table) and "plade" (board).

en boremaskine.explanation: "En boremaskine" means "a drill". It is built from "at bore" (to drill) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you drill a hole, say "Jeg borer et hul i væggen" (I am drilling a hole in the wall).

en borg.explanation: "En borg" means "a castle". Do not mix it up with "et slot" (a palace). To say a count lives in a castle, say "Greven bor i en borg" (The count lives in a castle). To say a king lives in a palace, say "Kongen bor på et slot" (The king lives in a palace).

en borger.explanation: "En borger" means "a citizen". A municipality calls the people it serves "borgere": "Kommunen hjælper borgerne" (The municipality helps the citizens).

en borgmester.explanation: "En borgmester" means "a mayor". To say someone is running for mayor, say "Hun stiller op som borgmester" (She is running for mayor). In Copenhagen the title is longer, "en overborgmester" (a lord mayor): "Københavns overborgmester holder tale" (Copenhagen's lord mayor gives a speech).

en bosætning.explanation: "En bosætning" means "a settlement". It is built from the verb "at bosætte sig" (to settle down), so it also means the act of settling: "Familien overvejer bosætning i Jylland" (The family is considering settling in Jutland).

en botanisk have.explanation: "En botanisk have" means "a botanical garden". Copenhagen has a well-known one called "Botanisk Have".

en bowlinghal.explanation: "En bowlinghal" means "a bowling alley". The ending "hal" (hall) is also in "en svømmehal" (an indoor swimming pool) and "en idrætshal" (a sports hall).

en bradepande.explanation: "En bradepande" means "a roasting pan". Do not mix it up with "en stegepande" (a frying pan). A roasting pan goes in the oven: "Kyllingen står i bradepanden" (The chicken is in the roasting pan). A frying pan goes on the stove: "Jeg steger æg i stegepanden" (I fry eggs in the frying pan).

en branche.explanation: "En branche" means "an industry". To say what field you work in, add "-branchen": "Hun arbejder i it-branchen" (She works in the IT industry).

en brand.explanation: "En brand" means "a fire (blaze)". To say a fire starts, use "at bryde ud" (to break out): "Der brød en brand ud i nat" (A fire broke out last night). To talk about a small fire you light on purpose, say "et bål" (a campfire): "Vi tænder et bål" (We light a campfire).

en brandalarm.explanation: "En brandalarm" means "a fire alarm". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "alarm" (alarm). To say the alarm is sounding, use "at gå" (to go): "Brandalarmen går" (The fire alarm is going off).

en brandbil.explanation: "En brandbil" means "a fire truck". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "bil" (car). In Denmark you call 112 for a fire truck: "Ring til 112, hvis det brænder" (Call 112 if something is on fire).

en brandmand.explanation: "En brandmand" means "a firefighter". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "mand" (man). To say they put out a fire, use "at slukke" (to put out): "Brandmændene slukker branden" (The firefighters put out the fire).

en brandslukker.explanation: "En brandslukker" means "a fire extinguisher". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "at slukke" (to put out). The verb "at slukke" also means to switch off: "Jeg slukker lyset" (I turn off the light).

en brandstation.explanation: "En brandstation" means "a fire station". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "station", the same word as in "en togstation" (a train station).

en brandtrappe.explanation: "En brandtrappe" means "a fire escape". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "en trappe" (a staircase). To say you left a building this way, say "Vi gik ned ad brandtrappen" (We went down the fire escape).

en bredde.explanation: "En bredde" means "a width". It comes from the adjective "bred" (wide). When you name length and width together, length comes first: "længde og bredde" (length and width).

en bregne.explanation: "En bregne" means "a fern". Do not mix it up with "et mos" (a moss). A fern grows in the shade: "Bregnen trives i skyggen" (The fern thrives in the shade). Moss grows on stone: "Der vokser mos på stenen" (Moss grows on the stone).

en bremse.explanation: "En bremse" means "a brake". The verb is "at bremse" (to brake): "Jeg bremser for rødt lys" (I brake for a red light). A different meaning of the same word is "a horsefly", an insect: "En bremse stak mig" (A horsefly stung me).

en brevkasse.explanation: "En brevkasse" means "a mailbox". It also means "an advice column" in a newspaper or magazine: "Brevkassen i bladet svarer på spørgsmål om kærlighed" (The advice column in the magazine answers questions about love).

en brevsprække.explanation: "En brevsprække" means "a mail slot". It is built from "brev" (letter) and "sprække" (slit). The word "sprække" also means a crack, as in "en sprække i muren" (a crack in the wall).

en brik.explanation: "En brik" means "a piece", as in a piece you move in a board game. To name a tile in Scrabble, use "en scrabblebrik" (a Scrabble tile).

en brise.explanation: "En brise" means "a breeze". A very common phrase is "en frisk brise" (a fresh breeze): "Der er en frisk brise i dag" (There is a fresh breeze today).

en brite.explanation: "En brite" means "a Brit". It comes from "Storbritannien" (Great Britain). Danish nationality words are not capitalized, so "brite" starts with a lowercase b: "Han er brite" (He is a Brit).

en bro.explanation: "En bro" means "a bridge". Denmark has famous bridges, such as "Øresundsbroen" (the Øresund Bridge) between Denmark and Sweden.

en brochure.explanation: "En brochure" means "a brochure". It is borrowed from French.

en brownie.explanation: "En brownie" means "a brownie". It is borrowed from English. To say you want one with ice cream, say "en brownie med is" (a brownie with ice cream): "Jeg vil gerne have en brownie med is" (I would like a brownie with ice cream).

en browser.explanation: "En browser" means "a browser". It is borrowed from English. To say you update it, use "at opdatere" (to update): "Prøv at opdatere din browser" (Try updating your browser).

en brudekjole.explanation: "En brudekjole" means "a wedding dress". It is built from "en brud" (a bride) and "en kjole" (a dress). To say someone is trying them on, say "Hun prøver brudekjoler i dag" (She is trying on wedding dresses today).

en brudepige.explanation: "En brudepige" means "a bridesmaid". It is built from "en brud" (a bride) and "en pige" (a girl).

en brudgom.explanation: "En brudgom" means "a groom". To talk about the bride and groom together, use "et brudepar" (a bridal couple): "Brudeparret danser først" (The bridal couple dance first).

en bruger.explanation: "En bruger" means "a user". It is built from "at bruge" (to use). The verb also means to spend: "Jeg bruger for mange penge" (I spend too much money).

en brugsanvisning.explanation: "En brugsanvisning" means "a user manual". It is built from "brug" (use) and "anvisning" (instruction). To tell someone to read it, say "Læs brugsanvisningen, før du starter maskinen" (Read the manual before you start the machine).

en brunch.explanation: "En brunch" means "a brunch". It is borrowed from English. Do not mix it up with "morgenmad" (breakfast): "Jeg spiser morgenmad klokken syv" (I eat breakfast at seven o'clock).

en brunkage.explanation: "En brunkage" means "a Danish spice cookie". It is built from "brun" (brown) and "en kage" (a cake). In Denmark it is a Christmas cookie: "Vi bager brunkager til jul" (We bake brunkager for Christmas).

en brunsviger.explanation: "En brunsviger" means "a Funen brown-sugar cake". It comes from the island of Funen (Fyn). The first part "brun" (brown) is also in "en brunkage" (a Danish spice cookie).

en bruser.explanation: "En bruser" means "a shower". To say you take a shower, use "et brusebad" (a shower bath): "Jeg tager et brusebad" (I take a shower).

en bryllupsdag.explanation: "En bryllupsdag" means "a wedding anniversary". It also means the day of the wedding itself, as in "Han er en glad brudgom på sin bryllupsdag" (He is a happy groom on his wedding day).

en bryllupsrejse.explanation: "En bryllupsrejse" means "a honeymoon". It is built from "bryllup" (wedding) and "rejse" (journey).

en brændenælde.explanation: "En brændenælde" means "a stinging nettle". It is built from "at brænde" (to burn) and "en nælde" (a nettle).

en brødkniv.explanation: "En brødkniv" means "a bread knife". It is built from "brød" (bread) and "kniv" (knife).

en brødkurv.explanation: "En brødkurv" means "a bread basket". It is built from "brød" (bread) and "kurv" (basket).

en brødrister.explanation: "En brødrister" means "a toaster". It is built from "brød" (bread) and "at riste" (to toast).

en brøk.explanation: "En brøk" means "a fraction". To name the parts of a fraction, say "en tæller" (a numerator) for the top number and "en nævner" (a denominator) for the bottom number.

en brønd.explanation: "En brønd" means "a well". To say people dig one, use "at grave" (to dig): "De graver en brønd i haven" (They are digging a well in the garden). The word is also used for oil, as in "en oliebrønd" (an oil well).

en buffet.explanation: "En buffet" means "a buffet". To say there is a buffet at a meal, the word needs no "en": "Der er buffet til frokost" (There is a buffet for lunch).
